server.pullQueued_other: {{count}} images are being pulled. A container uses a new image once it is recreated, such as by its stack's deploy.
server.noChecks: The agent has not reported any self-check yet.
server.removeHostNote: This revokes the agent's certificate and removes the server from the panel. Its containers keep running.

server.updateStepRolledBack: Rolled back to the old container

connect.title: Connect a new server
connect.descriptionBefore: The agent runs as a Docker container and connects out to
connect.descriptionAfter: . No port needs to be opened on the server, so this also works behind NAT.
connect.nameInvalid: Use lower case letters, digits and dashes.
connect.name: Name (lower case letters, digits, dashes)
connect.step2: 2 · Run the agent on the server
connect.tokenExpired: The token has expired. Tokens are valid for 15 minutes.
connect.composeNote: After enrollment PocketCloud owns the agent's updates: running this file again would bring back the old image.
connect.mountsNote: The Docker socket is needed to manage containers. The host's root is mounted read-only, for metrics and backups. The agent's identity stays in the pocketcloud-agent volume.
connect.happens1: The agent container generates its own key and sends a certificate request with the token.
connect.happens2: The panel checks the token, signs the certificate with its internal CA and retires the token.
connect.happens3: The agent opens an mTLS stream and waits for commands. No password is stored on disk.
connect.happens4: It sends the Docker inventory, and the server appears in the overview.
connect.happens5: The identity stays in the pocketcloud-agent volume, so it survives a restart and an update of the container.
connect.reqDocker: 24+ (the agent itself runs in a container)
connect.reqNetworkValue: outgoing TCP to the panel's gRPC port
connect.reqRootValue: The root file system must be a shared mount, as systemd sets it up. Without systemd, run at every boot:
connect.checkWaitingNote: usually within seconds of running the command
connect.checkCertNote: internal CA · valid for 180 days, rotates by itself
connect.updaterNote: A temporary pocketcloud-updater container does the update: it pulls the new image, swaps the agent container, and restores the old one if the new agent does not connect.
connect.notPinned: This development build does not know the digests of its agent images, so it cannot update agents.
connect.updateStarted_other: Updating {{count}} agents, one at a time.

audit.title: Change audit
audit.description: Every configuration change, from the UI, the API, the scheduler, agents and the PocketBase dashboard, with its author and the difference in values. Entries can only be added, and they are hash-chained.
audit.unsealed_one: The newest entry is not sealed yet
audit.unsealed_other: The newest {{count}} entries are not sealed yet
audit.unsealedNote: Written by a command that ran without the master key. The panel seals them when it starts with the key.
audit.shown: Showing {{shown}} of {{total}} · older entries load as you scroll
audit.revertNote: Reverting creates a new change, which is audited as well. Secrets are not restored.

diag.unavailableText: The diagnostics plugin is disabled on this panel, or the panel cannot be reached.
diag.description: Agent connections, gRPC messages, the command queue and the panel's internals. The data is only kept in memory, for 24 hours.
diag.messagesNote: both directions, over the time window
diag.queueNote: {{timeouts}} timeouts · {{replays}} replays since the panel started
diag.connectionsNote: select an agent for its details and message trace
diag.noAgentsText: Agents appear here once they connect, and are forgotten when the panel restarts.
diag.stripLabel: Connection of {{name}} over the last 24 hours
diag.noConnectionEvents: No connection events since the panel started.

reason.keepalive_timeout: keepalive timeout, the network may be down

diag.noRuntime: The agent has not reported its state yet.
diag.debugQueued: Debug logging is on for 15 minutes.
diag.captureStarted: Payloads are captured for 10 minutes. Sensitive fields stay masked.
diag.traceNote: Only metadata is kept: the last 500 messages per agent. Payloads are captured only on request, and sensitive fields are always masked.
diag.noErrors: No errors since the panel started

terminal.title: Web terminal
terminal.note: For administrators. Who opened it, when and where is recorded under Audit & activity; what is typed is not.
terminal.hostShellRisk: A host shell runs through a short-lived privileged container with full access to this server: anyone who gets here has root.
terminal.hostShellOff: Host shells are off on this server. To allow them, start its agent with HOST_SHELL_ENABLED=1.

stacks.name: Name (lower case letters, digits, dashes)
stacks.nameInvalid: Use lower case letters, digits, dashes and underscores.
stacks.noneText: A stack is a Compose project on one server: a file, its variables and its secrets, with every change kept as a revision.
stacks.foundNote: Compose projects that no stack manages yet
stacks.importQueued: Importing {{name}}. The stack appears here when its files have been read.
stacks.noComposeFile: Docker does not say which Compose file started it, so it cannot be imported.

stack.downNote: The stack and its revisions stay, and its named volumes too unless you say otherwise. Deploying brings the containers back.
stack.downVolumes: Also remove its named volumes, with their data
stack.saved: The changes were saved as a new revision.
stack.rollbackNote: This deploys the files of that revision as a new revision. The history only grows; secrets keep their current values.
stack.secretsNote: Secrets are stored encrypted and go to the agent inside the deploy command only. They are written to the env file during the deploy and removed afterwards, and cannot be read back.
stack.secretNameInvalid: Letters, digits and underscores; not starting with a digit.
stack.secretSaved: The secret was saved. It takes effect with the next deploy.
stack.removeNote: This removes the stack and its history from the panel. Its containers must be gone first.
stack.hostOffline: The server is offline: what you start now waits until it is back, for up to an hour.

db.title: Databases
db.description: Shared database servers on every host. Each application gets a database and a user with rights on it only, not the whole instance.
db.newServerNote: A shared server runs in its own stack, publishes no ports and gets a memory setting from the host's RAM.
db.newDatabaseNote: The database gets a user of the same name with rights on it only. Its password stays a secret of the panel.
db.kpiBackupsNote: a dump of every database, with milestone M4
db.noServersText: Create a shared server for the applications of a host. Database containers inside stacks show up here by themselves.
db.keepDedicated: Own extensions: stays on its own
db.notLinked: Link its credentials to see its databases
db.serverNameInvalid: Use lower case letters, digits and dashes.
db.serverQueued: Creating {{name}}: the image is pulled and the server started.
db.databaseNameInvalid: Start with a letter, then lower case letters, digits and underscores.
db.privateNetworks: a private network for each application
db.noDatabases: No databases on this server yet
db.noDatabasesText: A new database comes with its own user and, for a stack, the variables to reach it.
db.grantsText: only the database {{name}} · no rights on the others
db.rotateNote: A rotation updates the application's secret and restarts the application.
db.rotateQueued: The password is being changed; the application restarts with the new one.
db.adminerStarted: Adminer opens in a new tab and is removed after 30 minutes.
db.exportQueued: The dump is being made; it appears under Dumps when it is ready.
db.connectQueued: The stack gets its variables and its network to the server.
db.dropNote: Its user goes too, and so do the variables PocketCloud added to its stack, as a new revision. A final dump stays in the panel for 30 days; nothing is dropped if it cannot be kept.
db.statsQueued: The server is asked for its numbers.
db.sharedText: It serves the applications on {{host}}: each connects through a network of its own, without open ports and without access to the other applications. A new database gets its own user here.
db.dedicatedText: It runs inside an application's stack, on that stack's network.
db.moveText: Its databases can move to {{name}} on the same host. The application stops for a minute or two while its data is dumped and restored there, and keeps its user and password. That saves one instance.
db.moveKeep: The old container stays stopped for 7 days, so that you can go back; then the panel removes it. Its volume stays until you remove it.
db.moveConfirmText: {{stack}} stops while its data moves to {{name}}. Then it is deployed again and finds {{name}} under the name {{service}}, so its settings stay as they are. If anything fails, nothing changes and the stack starts again on its own server.
db.moving: Databases are moving from {{source}} to {{name}}. Their application is stopped until they are there.
db.oldKept: The old container stays stopped until {{date}}; its data volume stays.
db.oldRemoved: Moved on {{date}}; the old container is removed, its volume stays.
db.appPasswordNote: This database came from the application's own server: its password stays in the stack's settings, so the panel does not rotate it.
db.moveDatabaseText: For a newer version: {{stack}} stops while the database is dumped and restored on {{name}} with its user and password. Then its variables name {{name}} and it is deployed again.
db.moveTogetherText_one: For a newer version: {{stack}} stops while {{databases}} is dumped and restored on {{name}} with its user and password. {{stack}} reaches it as {{alias}}, and {{name}} will answer to that name.
db.moveTogetherText_other: For a newer version: {{stack}} reaches its databases here as {{alias}}, which can lead to one server only, so {{databases}} move to {{name}} together, with their users and passwords. {{stack}} stops meanwhile, and {{name}} will answer to that name.
db.movingDatabase: This database is moving to another server.
db.keepText: It needs {{extensions}}, which a shared server does not have, so it stays on its own.
db.updateText: The newest {{image}} is pulled and the container recreated with the same data. Applications lose their connections for a few seconds. The major version stays the same.
db.updateTextMariadb: The newest {{image}} is pulled and the container recreated with the same data; MariaDB upgrades its system tables as it starts. Applications lose their connections for a few seconds.
db.majorNote: PostgreSQL {{version}} is a new major version: create a server with it and move the databases there one by one, each with a short stop of its application.
db.linkText: A database container of the stack {{stack}}. With its administrator's credentials the panel reads its databases and connections; the password stays a secret of the panel.
db.dumpsNote: SQL exports for 7 days, final dumps of dropped databases for 30
db.ownCredentials: the stack {{name}} holds its users and passwords
